html:
The Assam Company, founded in 1839, was the first company to grow tea commercially in India, and the start of the plantation economy of Assam.

It was formed in London and Calcutta soon after the Assam tea plant was identified. It took over most of the government's experimental tea gardens. The early years went badly, and the company nearly failed in the 1840s. By the 1850s it was making profits, which set off a rush of new tea companies and a speculative bubble in the 1860s.

The plantations needed many hands, and few local people wanted the work. Planters brought in labourers from the Chota Nagpur plateau and other poor regions of central and eastern India, under contracts much like Indian indenture. Conditions on the gardens were hard, and workers who ran away could be punished by law.

The company outlived British rule. Its success led planters on to Darjeeling and to Ceylon, making the British Empire the world's largest tea supplier and ending China's hold on the trade.
sum: The Assam Company, founded in 1839, was the first company to grow tea commercially in India, and the start of the plantation economy of Assam.
